overview: Eso & Kechizu’s settings tune summon orders, the decay beam, and its cameras. Solo Eso shares these rows.
technicalOverview: Eso & Kechizu (CP_160) is a playable death-painting character whose kit is built around one summoned shikigami (CN_080) and a rot/decay branch. The character row points at nine unique-table slots; seven are populated here (main tuning, shikigami-command tuning, decay-beam tuning, decay range/upkeep, and three decay-shot camera rows) and the last two are empty. All traced reads go through AGameCharacter::GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue / FGameCharacterAction::GetOwnerUniqueFloat, which dereference UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] without bounds checks; UniqueRows is built in the order of CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterUnique. The traced readers include the CP_160 controller, its action classes, and the shared helpers they call. A zero is not itself evidence that a slot is unused: indices under "untraced" simply had no CP_160 read identified after searching the source, and the nonzero slot 6 of CP_160_ATTACKG is called out explicitly as unresolved.

CP_160.title: Eso & Kechizu - main tuning row
CP_160.overview: General settings for the summon: how close CN_080 must stay, how fast automatic and manual shikigami orders fire, their reach and lifetimes, and the energy cost of the manual order.

0.label: Beam growth speed multiplier
0.simple: When the shikigami is missing or still alive, the decay beam grows about 1.65 times faster; once the shikigami is defeated, growth is normal.
0.technical: AddBeam starts Factor at 1.0 and replaces it with UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[0] only when GetShikigami(0) is null OR that shikigami's IsDefeated() returns false (alive). A defeated shikigami leaves Factor at 1.0. The stored Entry.Rate is Factor * Rate; TickBeams advances Progress by the time-scaled tick times that Rate.

1.label: Summon leash / auto-order distance
1.simple: The summon will not attack on its own if it drifts more than 1200 units from Eso; the same distance limits which enemies can be chosen.
1.technical: TickAutoAttack reads UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[1] as Range. It requires the owner-to-shikigami Delta.Size() <= Range (skips when > Range), and filters opponent characters by Distance > Range from the owner. Equality passes both checks; there is no negative/unlimited special case on this value.

2.label: Auto-order wind-up time
2.simple: After a target is found, the automatic shikigami order waits about 1.25 seconds before it is issued.
2.technical: TickAutoAttack adds the time-scaled tick to AutoAttackTime once a valid target exists and returns while UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[2] > AutoAttackTime. The order fires on the first tick with AutoAttackTime >= 1.25; the timer is then zeroed.

3.label: Auto-order cooldown
3.simple: Once the shikigami has been ordered automatically, about 4 seconds pass before the next automatic order.
3.technical: AutoAttackCooldown is assigned UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[3] when the order is placed; each tick subtracts the scaled DeltaTime while it is > 0, and the start gate `!(AutoAttackCooldown <= 0)` blocks until it is zero or negative. On shikigami summon-cooldown restart it is instead set to -1.0f, bypassing the wait.

4.label: Auto-order trigger radius
4.simple: A normal auto-order tells CN_080 to commit to its queued attack once it is within 500 units of the target.
4.technical: TickAutoAttack reads UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[4] into Value194 and passes it as the third argument of UCN_080_ActionController::SetTargetMode(2, Action, Value194, Value198, -1.0f). Traced into SetTargetMode: Value194 becomes QueuedActionRadius; CN_080::ActionTick compares squared shikigami-to-target distance against radius*radius (a negative radius disables the trigger).

5.label: Auto-order mode time limit
5.simple: A normal auto-order keeps its follow/target mode for about 3 seconds.
5.technical: TickAutoAttack reads UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[5] into Value198 (fourth SetTargetMode argument). SetTargetMode stores it as TargetModeTimeLimit; CN_080::ActionTick counts it down while >= 0 and calls ResetTargetMode when it drops below zero and no attack is active.

6.label: Manual-order distance (neutral stick)
6.simple: Holding the manual-order key with no stick direction works only while the summon is within 1200 units of Eso.
6.technical: TickOrderAttack reads UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[6] as Range and returns when `Range >= 0 && Delta.Size() > Range`, with Delta measured from the shikigami to the owner. Negative values would skip the distance gate entirely; with 1200, equality passes and larger distances refuse the order.

7.label: Manual-order trigger radius (stick up)
7.simple: With the stick held up, the manual order commits CN_080 to its heavy attack within 750 units rather than 500.
7.technical: TickOrderAttack switches Action from Attack_3 to Attack_4 on stick up and replaces Value194 with UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[7]; SetTargetMode then stores it as QueuedActionRadius (same squared-distance trigger, negative disables).

8.label: Manual-order mode time limit (stick up)
8.simple: With the stick held up, the issued order keeps its target mode for about 2 seconds.
8.technical: In the stick-up branch TickOrderAttack replaces Value198 with UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[8]; SetTargetMode stores it as TargetModeTimeLimit, counted down while >= 0 before ResetTargetMode.

9.label: Manual-order distance (stick up)
9.simple: The up-stick manual order is allowed from a slightly farther summon distance (1200 units).
9.technical: TickOrderAttack replaces AttackSetId with CP_160_ATTACKG_2 on stick up and Range with UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[9]; the same `Range >= 0 && Delta.Size() > Range` refusal applies before the attack-set row is looked up.

10.label: Manual-order energy cost multiplier
10.simple: The manual order multiplies the chosen attack's cursed-energy cost by 2, then adds it to the current energy before the affordability check.
10.technical: TickOrderAttack computes CursedEnergy = UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[10] * AttackRow->CursedEnergy_Add + StatusController->CursedEnergy (from the CP_160_ATTACKG/_2 row's first attack). If bNotForce and the result is < 0 the order is refused; otherwise the computed value is written back with SetCursedEnergy, so a positive CursedEnergy_Add is spent and a negative one restored.

notes.text: The energy multiplier is applied to the attack row reached through the unique-table range check, and the resulting energy value is written back only after the order succeeds; the affordability check itself uses the same multiplied expression.

CP_160_ATTACKG.title: Cursed-energy shikigami command (ATTACKG) tuning
CP_160_ATTACKG.overview: Distances and command timings used when Eso spends cursed energy to order the shikigami; the stick direction selects which sub-values are used.

0.label: CE-1 command trigger radius
0.simple: The normal cursed-energy shikigami command commits the attack within 500 units.
0.technical: TCP_160_CursedEnergyAttack_1::StartAttackHoming reads UniqueRows[1]->FloatValue[0] into Value194 by default and passes it to CN_080 SetTargetMode(Mode=2 or 1, Decay byte, Value194, Value198, 1.0f). Value194 is the shikigami's QueuedActionRadius; the queued action triggers only while the shikigami-to-target distance is strictly less than the radius.

1.label: CE-1 command time limit
1.simple: The normal cursed-energy command keeps its target mode for about 3 seconds.
1.technical: UniqueRows[1]->FloatValue[1] becomes Value198, stored as CN_080 TargetModeTimeLimit; it counts down from >= 0 and resets the mode when it goes negative while no attack is active.

2.label: CE-1 normal attack-set range
2.simple: The neutral-stick cursed-energy order uses the standard attack set only when the summon is within 2000 units; otherwise the fallback set is used.
2.technical: GetAttackSetRow first requires shikigami 0 alive, CanOrderAttack and a valid owner target. It then reads UniqueRows[1]->FloatValue[2] as Range and sets bFallback when `Range >= 0 && shikigami-to-owner Distance > Range`; on fallback it looks up CP_160_ATTACKG_5. Equality passes.

3.label: CE-1 up-stick trigger radius
3.simple: With the stick up the cursed-energy command uses a 750-unit trigger radius.
3.technical: UniqueRows[1]->FloatValue[3] replaces Value194 when IsLeftStickInDirection(0, 45.0001, 0.5) is true; it is passed to SetTargetMode as QueuedActionRadius and the shikigami's queued Attack_4 fires inside that radius.

4.label: CE-1 up-stick time limit
4.simple: With the stick up the cursed-energy command keeps its target mode for about 3 seconds.
4.technical: UniqueRows[1]->FloatValue[4] replaces Value198 in the stick-up branch of StartAttackHoming; SetTargetMode stores it as TargetModeTimeLimit.

5.label: CE-1 up-stick attack-set range
5.simple: The up-stick cursed-energy order allows the standard attack set out to 2000 units.
5.technical: GetAttackSetRow reads UniqueRows[1]->FloatValue[5] as Range in the stick-up branch (attack set CP_160_ATTACKG_2) and applies the same `Range >= 0 && Distance > Range` fallback rule to CP_160_ATTACKG_5.

6.label: Unresolved sixth command value
6.simple: This nonzero slot (500) has no identified CP_160 read in the reconstructed source.
6.technical: The CE-1 command path reads only value indices 0, 1, 3 and 4 (StartAttackHoming) and 2, 5 and 7 (GetAttackSetRow); the manual/auto order helpers read row 1 values 0, 1, 3 and 4 as well. No shared CP_160-reachable caller was found for UniqueRows[1]->FloatValue[6]. The nearest similarly-sized value, row 1 value 0, is a 500-unit command radius, but that is not evidence that slot 6 is another radius.

7.label: CE-1 down-stick attack-set range
7.simple: With the stick down the cursed-energy order never falls back for distance: the stored -1 means unlimited range.
7.technical: GetAttackSetRow reads UniqueRows[1]->FloatValue[7] as Range in the stick-down branch (attack set CP_160_ATTACKG_4). The fallback test is guarded by `Range >= 0`, so -1 removes the distance restriction; the separate stick-down command sets Value194/Value198 to a literal -1.0f and Mode=1, not from this slot.

notes.text: CP_160_ATTACKG in this unique table is not the AttackSet row of the same name: the former supplies the ranges that decide whether the latter (or its _2, _4, _5 variants) is looked up.

CP_160_ATTACKH.title: Decay shot beams (ATTACKH) tuning
CP_160_ATTACKH.overview: Three level-based sets for the decay projectiles: aim limit, growth speed and maximum length, plus the repeat interval used while holding the level-3 charge.

0.label: Beam aim angle, level 1
0.simple: At cursed-energy level 1 the shot can bend about 40 degrees toward the secondary target.
0.technical: OnEffectPlayed handles FX_CP_160_08111/21/31. For level 1 (also the default branch) UniqueRows[2]->FloatValue[0] is MaxAngle; it clamps the planar aim yaw to [-MaxAngle, MaxAngle] with a NaN-to--MaxAngle quirk, and is passed as both limits of GameAnimNotify_ClampedElevation for pitch. The auto action types 75/79 overwrite MaxAngle with 90 degrees, ignoring this slot there.

1.label: Beam aim angle, level 2
1.simple: At level 2 the beam uses its own 40-degree aim limit.
1.technical: Level 2 of the same switch reads UniqueRows[2]->FloatValue[1] as MaxAngle and feeds the same yaw/elevation clamps; auto variants still force 90 degrees.

2.label: Beam aim angle, level 3
2.simple: At level 3 the beam uses its own 40-degree aim limit.
2.technical: Level 3 reads UniqueRows[2]->FloatValue[2] as MaxAngle for the yaw clamp and both elevation limits before the auto-variant 90-degree override.

3.label: Beam growth rate, level 1
3.simple: Level 1 beams grow roughly 2800 units of progress per second before the summon-status multiplier.
3.technical: UniqueRows[2]->FloatValue[3] is Rate for level 1; AddBeam stores Factor * Rate in Entry.Rate, and TickBeams advances Progress by the scaled DeltaTime times Rate, clamped at MaxProgress.

4.label: Beam growth rate, level 2
4.simple: Level 2 beams use their own 2800-unit growth rate.
4.technical: UniqueRows[2]->FloatValue[4] is the level 2 Rate passed to AddBeam and multiplied by the beam Factor; growth uses the same time-scaled tick.

5.label: Beam growth rate, level 3
5.simple: Level 3 beams use their own 2800-unit growth rate.
5.technical: UniqueRows[2]->FloatValue[5] is the level 3 Rate; it follows the same AddBeam/TickBeams path as the lower levels.

6.label: Beam maximum length, level 1
6.simple: Level 1 beams stop extending at about 2000 units.
6.technical: UniqueRows[2]->FloatValue[6] is MaxProgress for level 1. TickBeams clamps Progress with FMath::Min(MaxProgress, Grown) and floors negative growth at 0; Progress is sent to Niagara as BeamEndPoint and to the capsule/destructible-mesh trace.

7.label: Beam maximum length, level 2
7.simple: Level 2 beams stop extending at about 2500 units.
7.technical: UniqueRows[2]->FloatValue[7] is the level 2 MaxProgress passed to AddBeam; the same inclusive clamp caps beam growth and the Niagara/trace end point.

8.label: Beam maximum length, level 3
8.simple: Level 3 beams stop extending at about 3000 units.
8.technical: UniqueRows[2]->FloatValue[8] is the level 3 MaxProgress; on beam finish the recorded Progress is also used when spawning the follow-up effect at the beam transform.

9.label: Level-3 charge repeat interval
9.simple: While the level-3 charge is held, it re-pays the attack cost and replays the animation every 0.3 seconds.
9.technical: In the level-3 / start-count-1 charge branch, TickAttack requires flag158, an affordable cost and key 9 held, then accumulates DeltaTime and returns while ActionElapsedTime <= UniqueRows[2]->FloatValue[9]. Only when elapsed is strictly greater than 0.3 does it call SetCursedEnergy, zero the timer, clear flag158 and replay Animation; otherwise flag159 is set on release/failure.

notes.text: Level 1 is also the default branch of the OnEffectPlayed switch, so a level outside 1..3 reads slot 0/3/6 rather than treating the shot as disabled.
The auto variants of the cursed-energy attack (types 75/79) discard the row's aim angle and use a literal 90 degrees, so the 40-degree values only shape the manually aimed shots.

CP_160_ATTACKH_2.title: Decay state range and upkeep (ATTACKH_2)
CP_160_ATTACKH_2.overview: Two settings for the rot/decay branch: how far away a decayed opponent still counts, and how much cursed energy the branch drains each second.

0.label: Decay target search range
0.simple: Decayed opponents farther than this from Eso are ignored; the stored -1 means no distance limit.
0.technical: GetDecayingOpponents filters opponents carrying Decay_1..3 (or RotTechnique when decay mode is off) and reads UniqueRows[3]->FloatValue[0] as Range. It skips a character when `Range >= 0 && Delta.Size() > Range`; a negative value disables the check. This list gates both the decay detonation and the ATTACKH_2/_3 attack sets.

1.label: Decay-mode cursed energy drain
1.simple: While rot decay is active, Eso loses about 12 cursed energy per second before the normal recovery step.
1.technical: GetCursedEnergyDrainRate returns 0.0f when bDecayMode == 0 and UniqueRows[3]->FloatValue[1] otherwise. AGameCharacter::GetActionValue113 forwards it to the status tick, which calls SetCursedEnergy(CursedEnergy - Drain * DeltaTime) when Drain >= 0; regular recovery is applied afterwards in the same tick.

notes.text: Switching decay mode off strips Decay_1/2/3 from every opponent, so the drain returns to zero and the decay-specific attack sets stop being selected.

CP_160_ATTACKH_SHOOT_CAMERA_1.title: Decay shot camera, level 1
CP_160_ATTACKH_SHOOT_CAMERA_1.overview: Framing for the level-1 cursed-energy decay shot: offset, look limits, field of view and orbit.

0.label: Camera offset - sideways
0.simple: The camera sits 220 units to the side of the usual eye position.
0.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest(2, RowIndex) reads UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[0] as CameraOffset.X. The camera applies this FVector after rotating it into the gaze rotation's space, so it is a gaze-relative camera offset, not a world-X teleport.

1.label: Camera offset - depth
1.simple: The camera is pulled 180 units back along the gaze axis.
1.technical: Value index 1 becomes CameraOffset.Y in the same FVector; its sign and effect follow the gaze-relative basis described above.

2.label: Camera offset - height
2.simple: The camera is raised 100 units above the gaze-based eye position.
2.technical: Value index 2 is read first into OffsetZ and becomes CameraOffset.Z of the request.

3.label: Downward gaze limit
3.simple: The camera will not look more than about 60 degrees below the eye line for this shot.
3.technical: Value index 3 becomes LimitAngleDown. UpdateRequestCamera computes the gaze elevation in degrees and, when the target is below the base, rotates the gaze back within this limit; equality with the measured angle passes.

4.label: Upward gaze limit
4.simple: The camera will not look more than about 30 degrees above the eye line for this shot.
4.technical: Value index 4 becomes LimitAngleUp and is used by the same degree-based elevation clamp when the target is above the base.

5.label: Field of view
5.simple: The row asks for a 110-degree field of view when the shot camera is entered; the restore paths replace it with a literal 90 degrees.
5.technical: Value index 5 becomes Request.FieldOfView. CP_160's OnEffectPlayed(IntParameter 10) and the level-3 second-start restore overwrite that field with 90.0f after building the request, and the final exit to AttackDefault uses a separate zeroed request with only FOV 90. The initial SetCameraMode(2, true, ...) calls use the row value unmodified.

6.label: Field-of-view blend time
6.simple: Changing to this field of view is blended over about 0.25 seconds.
6.technical: Value index 6 becomes FieldOfViewBlendTime; the request is passed to SetCameraMode with bBlendView true on entry and on the level-3/restore transitions. The final AttackDefault exit instead passes false and a request whose blend time is zero.

7.label: Field-of-view easing kind
7.simple: The stored 3 selects the EaseInOut curve for the field-of-view change.
7.technical: Value index 7 is cast to int32 in a switch: 0 -> Linear, 1 -> EaseIn, 2 -> EaseOut, 3 -> EaseInOut (EEasingFunc), and any other value leaves the request default. Here the value is exactly 3.

8.label: Gaze orbit yaw
8.simple: The camera orbits the gaze about the camera by 15 degrees of yaw.
8.technical: Value index 8 becomes Request.OrbitYaw; the virtual camera constructs FRotator(OrbitPitch, OrbitYaw, 0) and rotates the gaze around the camera through that transform.

9.label: Gaze orbit pitch
9.simple: The same orbit tilts the gaze by -7 degrees of pitch.
9.technical: Value index 9 becomes Request.OrbitPitch, the Pitch component of the FRotator used in the orbit step.

10.label: Camera roll
10.simple: The view is rolled by 2.5 units (the roll passed to the camera's view-target setter).
10.technical: Value index 10 becomes Request.Roll and is handed to SetViewTarget87 together with the computed camera position and gaze. No other CP_160 caller overrides it.

notes.text: Level 1 switches the owner to camera mode 2 with this row on the first start of the charged cursed-energy shot; the same row is reused by the level-1 restore path (or the third start at level 3).

Both accessors take the float index first and the row index second, despite the controller often naming the pair by effect first. The checked-free dereference means a read of one of CP_160's two null table slots (7 or 8) would be invalid; the traced CP_160 code stays within rows 0..6.

The decay branch has two modes. RotTechnique mode converts enemies to DEBUFF_DECAY_n and lets the charge detonate waist-level damage rows; after that the controller reads Decay_1..3 stacks, enables the cursed-energy drain from row 3 value 1, and selects CP_160_ATTACKH_2/_3 attack sets. Clearing decay mode strips the Decay buffs from opponents and disables the drain.

The summoned CN_080 has its own ShikigamiUniqueDataTable. Calls such as UCN_080_ActionController::GetMovementSpeedRate, its AttackH animation count and its beam length read AGameShikigami::GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue on the shikigami, not the seven character rows documented here.

Same-looking unique indices in other controllers are not reused here. The AI hold durations at GameCharacterAINode.cpp:112-130 are instantiated by CP_040's behavior controller, and the row-2/row-7/row-8 reads in GameTrapActionController sit inside CP_150 trap bodies; neither is attributable to CP_160. CP_160 itself has no dedicated behavior-controller class: AI type 17 uses the base behavior controller and the playable FGameCharacterAIThinkNode_CP_160.

The controller delegates part of its behavior: CP_030_ActionHelpers decides whether an order can start, CP_110_FindLayerAction checks the active attack layer, and CN_080 SetTargetMode receives the tuned radius/time values. It also defines the shared ParallelAttack finder that CP_140 calls; these are shared helpers, not CP_160-only mechanics.
